scope: Mini-review of G-CORE-6b PR #1328 (P-III autonomous SnapshotBlob.schema_version 1->2 + merkle_root: Option<Cid> v2 field per Ben no-users-yet 2026-05-22-night auth). 12 files / +451/-9 (281 of +451 = cherry-picked tf11 test file; net new ~170 LOC). 4 tf11 RED-PHASE pins: 1 un-ignored (W5 ARM-W5-1 forward-compat) + 2 inverted-by-design tripwires (constant-pin 1->2 + error-code-mapping Serialize->SnapshotBlobSchemaVersionMismatch) + 1 retained (strict-mismatch reject, forge target shifted +1=2 -> +1=3). +1 ErrorCode SnapshotBlobSchemaVersionMismatch (CATALOG 176->177 atomic Rust+TS+ERROR-CATALOG.md+stable_shape.rs). §8-B consumer wire-up named-now at docs/future/phase-4-backlog.md §8-B-merkle-range-proof-consumer-wire-up per HARD RULE 12 clause-(b). Per pim-canary heightened-scrutiny + §3.5n ground-truth verify.
summary: G-CORE-6b is a clean P-III autonomous in-place struct mutation that correctly implements the Ben no-users-yet override of the plan's G-CORE-9 P-III scheduling. The scope is genuinely surgical: SnapshotBlob gains exactly one v2 field (merkle_root: Option<Cid>) as a tail-append (preserving canonical-bytes shift to a single discriminant + single new field), the schema_version constant flips 1->2, the SchemaVersion error variant lifts from generic Serialize to typed SnapshotBlobSchemaVersionMismatch, and the engine snapshot path writes None pending §8-B materializer. The scaffolding-minimum decision (only merkle_root: Option<Cid>, NOT a speculative range_proof_metadata bytes field) is correct per the §8-B trait surface not yet existing — adding speculative fields would risk shape-lock without a working consumer. The 4 tf11 pin dispositions are all defensible: the constant-pin and error-code-mapping inversions are intentional updates of P-III tripwires that correctly fired on the bump (the test comments are explicit + the new assertions are still substantive). The 4 tf11 tests pass locally (verified by `cargo nextest run -p benten-graph --test tf11_...`: 4 passed, 0 skipped). The pre-existing benten-graph + benten-eval RED-PHASE test failures (sample_for_test / last_put_node_durability_for_label / tamper_mapping_for_test — all `cfg(any(test, feature = "testing"))`-gated helpers called from integration tests without the testing feature enabled) are GROUND-TRUTH VERIFIED to exist on main e89a1919 (verified by checkout + cargo check + observation of identical method-not-found errors). §3.5g cross-language mirror is atomic (Rust enum + TS errors.generated.ts class + CODE_TO_CTOR_GENERATED entry + CATALOG_CODES array + ERROR-CATALOG.md row + stable_shape.rs ALL_CATALOG_VARIANTS + catalog_variant_count_matches_enum exhaustive match + variant_count_is_pinned 176->177 + recoverability_classification all touched). INTERNALS.md updated for the v2 shape + schema-version-mismatch lift. The §8-B consumer wire-up backlog row at docs/future/phase-4-backlog.md is concrete (lists specific files + the likely future ErrorCode E_SNAPSHOT_BLOB_MERKLE_ROOT_MISMATCH) — a real BELONGS-NAMED-NOW destination, not a phantom carry. Author Benten-Ben, no AI attribution, PR opened NORMAL on base main, branch protection BLOCKED (expected, CI in-progress at write-time). Coordination collision with #1325 (both bump to 177) is expected per brief; second-merger rebases to 178+. One MINOR finding: the W5 ARM-W5-1 forward-compat test constructs a v1-discriminator blob using the V2 struct shape (5 fields including merkle_root: None) rather than a true 4-field v1-encoded fixture — the reader fully deserializes BEFORE checking the discriminator, so the test exercises the discriminator-strict-reject mechanism but does NOT exercise the true on-disk-v1-blob-handed-to-v2-reader scenario; acceptable per no-users-yet (a real v1 byte fixture would be hand-constructed CBOR + this test still verifies the load-bearing reject mechanism). One OBS: the plan body itself (00-implementation-plan.md §1.A.FROZEN item 4 / §8-F / G-CORE-6b group def) still describes this bump as 'P-III-scheduled at G-CORE-9, NOT landed autonomously' — the Ben 2026-05-22-night no-users-yet override is captured in the commit message + this brief but is not yet folded into the plan body. Plan-body retense is an orchestrator-direct follow-up, NOT a PR-author concern.

findings.lens: pim-18 §3.6f SHAPE-not-SUBSTANCE — W5 ARM-W5-1 forward-compat fixture realism
findings.claim: The W5 ARM-W5-1 forward-compat test (snapshot_blob_v2_reader_strict_rejects_v1_blob_forward_compat_direction) constructs a 'v1-discriminator' blob using the V2 struct shape — including the merkle_root: None tail-append field — and encodes via to_canonical_bytes(). A real pre-bump v1 producer would emit a 4-field struct (no merkle_root tail). Because SnapshotBlobBackend::from_bytes_with_cap calls SnapshotBlob::from_canonical_bytes FIRST (full deserialization) and THEN checks blob.schema_version, the test exercises the discriminator-strict-reject mechanism correctly but does NOT exercise the true on-disk-v1-blob-handed-to-v2-reader scenario the docstring claims (the test comment is actually explicit about this gap: 'canonical bytes differ in both the schema-version discriminator AND the tail-append-field absence... For this test the discriminator alone is enough to drive the strict-reject — the reader checks the discriminator before any structural validation of the trailing fields' — but the second half of that comment is INCORRECT: from_bytes does NOT check the discriminator before deserializing; it fully deserializes the bytes via serde_ipld_dagcbor::from_slice and then checks the field).
evidence: crates/benten-graph/src/backends/snapshot_blob.rs:323-340 (from_bytes_with_cap): step 1 = size-check, step 2 = SnapshotBlob::from_canonical_bytes(bytes) full deserialize, step 3 = check schema_version. The deserialize step would FAIL on a true 4-field v1 blob (serde_ipld_dagcbor map decode against a 5-field struct definition) — it would surface as SnapshotBlobError::Decode, NOT SchemaVersion.

crates/benten-graph/tests/tf11_snapshot_blob_schema_version_p3_migration_path.rs (ARM-W5-1) — constructs SnapshotBlob { schema_version: 1, anchor_cid: None, nodes: BTreeMap::new(), system_zone_index: BTreeMap::new(), merkle_root: None } (5 fields, V2 shape with v1 discriminator). The encoded bytes contain the merkle_root key.

Disposition impact: the strict-reject mechanism IS exercised correctly (a forged future-version blob in the existing snapshot_blob_schema_version_strict_mismatch_reject_is_the_documented_p3_migration_path test makes the equivalent forward-direction claim symmetric). The gap is that the W5 ARM-W5-1 fixture is not a faithful v1 emitter — it's a v2 struct with the discriminator field flipped to 1.
findings.disposition: DISAGREE-WITH-EXPLANATION (no fix required at this PR per no-users-yet rationale). A genuinely faithful v1 fixture would need to encode hand-rolled CBOR bytes (or snapshot bytes produced by the pre-bump build); the no-users-yet rationale that authorizes the bump itself also covers this test's reduced fidelity (there is no real on-disk v1 corpus to test against). The discriminator-strict-reject mechanism IS verified end-to-end, which IS the load-bearing property. Logging this finding so the gap is named: if a true v1 byte fixture were ever desired (e.g. for a future audit), the fix is hand-constructed CBOR bytes that omit the merkle_root field. Optional pre-merge fix: clarify the W5 ARM-W5-1 docstring/inline-comment that the reader fully deserializes BEFORE the discriminator check (the current comment overstates the reader's eager-discriminator behavior). Orchestrator-direct candidate; not blocking.

ground_truth_verify.v2_shape_scaffolding_appropriate: agreed — merkle_root: Option<Cid> only (no speculative range_proof_metadata bytes field) is the correct scaffolding decision given (1) the §8-B MerkleRangeProofBackend trait does not yet exist so the actual proof metadata shape is unknown, (2) any speculative field shape that locks at G-CORE-9 freeze without a working consumer creates a binding wire-format commitment that may not match the eventual trait's needs, (3) the Option<Cid> sentinel allows pre-§8-B blobs to encode None today without forcing a 2->3 bump when the consumer wave lands and starts populating the field (a producer that starts writing Some(mst_root) does NOT change the schema_version — the canonical bytes change is just None->Some, which is a value change not a shape change). The docs/future/phase-4-backlog.md §8-B-merkle-range-proof-consumer-wire-up row is a concrete BELONGS-NAMED-NOW destination (lists specific files + the likely future ErrorCode + the wave home options).
ground_truth_verify.tf11_inverted_pins_substantive: verified — both inverted-by-design pins (constant-pin snapshot_blob_schema_version_constant_is_2_after_g_core_6b_bump_landed + error-code-mapping snapshot_blob_schema_version_error_maps_to_typed_snapshot_blob_schema_version_mismatch_post_g_core_6b) still assert substantive properties post-bump, not rubber-stamping new values. The constant-pin asserts `==2` with a docstring naming the wave + the no-users-yet rationale + would-FAIL conditions (regression OR silent further bump without updating this pin). The error-code-mapping pin asserts SnapshotBlobError::SchemaVersion { expected, actual }.code() == ErrorCode::SnapshotBlobSchemaVersionMismatch (not Serialize) — this exercises the lift mechanism end-to-end and would catch (a) un-lifting back to a generic catch-all family, (b) reshaping the SnapshotBlobError variant identity without updating the mapping, (c) drift between Rust + TS-side error class names. Both pins are GREEN at HEAD (4 tf11 tests pass; verified via nextest 4-passed-0-skipped). The retained strict-mismatch reject pin (forge target shifted +1=2 -> +1=3) is still substantive — forges a future-version blob via to_canonical_bytes + asserts SnapshotBlobBackend::from_bytes strict-rejects with the right expected/actual values. The W5 ARM-W5-1 un-ignored pin IS the load-bearing forward-compat assertion (with the MINOR fixture-realism gap noted at g-core-6b-mr-1 — the strict-reject mechanism IS exercised; the fixture is a v2-struct-with-v1-discriminator rather than a faithful 4-field v1 emit).
ground_truth_verify.preexisting_failures_unrelated: verified — I checked out base e89a1919, ran `cargo +1.95 check -p benten-graph --tests --test capability_grant_writes_immediate` and observed identical 'method not found' errors for `tamper_mapping_for_test` on `tf3d_two_cid_mapping_roundtrip` test (same root-cause class: integration tests in tests/ use `cfg(any(test, feature = "testing"))`-gated helpers without enabling the testing feature on the dev-dep). The implementer-cited failing test families (sample_for_test in benten-eval/tests, derive_key_for_test elsewhere, last_put_node_durability_for_label in capability_grant_writes_immediate) are all the SAME PRE-EXISTING R3 RED-PHASE feature-gate class, completely orthogonal to G-CORE-6b's snapshot blob work. The implementer's §3.5n claim ('verified by git stash + workspace re-check') is structurally correct.
